notes: Provo, UTAH — Utah County seat, pop. 115,162, home to Brigham Young University. 18,700 shipped parcels, $5.26B land value / $16.31B total market value (2025 roll). Source: UGRC's statewide LIR parcel layer, Utah County sheet (services1.arcgis.com/99lidPhWCzftIe9K .../Parcels_Utah_LIR), clipped to the Utah Municipal Boundaries polygon for Provo. One-stop layer — geometry, land + total market value, acreage, property class and a 152-value building taxonomy all in one place. See run_provo.py.

VALUES ARE FULL MARKET VALUE, not Utah's 55% primary-residential taxable basis. Verified live against the assessor's own value history for two parcels (04:017:0017 and 04:002:0034): the LIR figures match the table headed 'Market Value' row-for-row for 2025. NOTE the assessor has already published 2026 values; the state LIR feed is one roll behind, so we ship 2025.

ONE ROW PER BUILDING, NOT PER PARCEL: 38,687 Provo rows collapse to 30,310 parcels, and one apartment complex (04:021:0031, 865 N 160 W) is 216 rows all carrying the SAME $23.3M total. The ETL dedups on PARCEL_ID taking values as `first` (never summed — skill §2), summing BLDG_SQFT and keeping the LARGEST building's type for classification.

NO EXEMPTION FIELD EXISTS. TAXEXEMPT_TYPE is NULL on every Utah County row and PROP_CLASS='Tax Exempt' covers just 25 parcels, because exempt land in Utah simply is not assessed — it carries NULL values. So 'no land value' IS the exemption flag here, and 5,865 parcels are excluded on it: whole 640-acre PLSS sections of Uinta National Forest in the mountains east of town, the municipal airport (828 acres), BYU, schools, parks, ROW and leftover HOA open space. Consequence: 0 zero-land parcels ship, so Provo has no gp-error layer.

CONDOS/PUDs ARE MERGED, not hidden (skill §6a/§6b, run_olympia.py recipe). Provo's student-housing stock is mapped as building-footprint stubs: 3,220 valued parcels under 1,000 sqft, with PARCEL_ACRES agreeing with the polygon (median ratio 1.001), so the assessor carries no independent land area for them either — the development's real land is a separate UNVALUED parcel in the same plat. Left alone they render as thousands of pencils at up to $351/sqft against a citywide median of $25. run_provo.py merges 5,652 unit stubs down onto their plat's common-area land, producing 293 development parcels at a median $18/sqft — right on the citywide median, which is the §6b calibration test. Rendered land $/sqft max drops 351 -> 350 citywide but p99 drops 115 -> 77.

THE MERGE GATE IS PLAT DOMINANCE, NOT ADJACENCY. Utah County serials are MM:PPP:LLLL and MM:PPP is the plat map, so a plat merges only when its sub-2,000-sqft valued stubs are >=60% of its valued parcels. That separates a pure condo/PUD regime (plat 37118: 120 stubs + one 3.9-acre common parcel, zero ordinary lots) from a MIXED subdivision (plat 36196: 8 stubs among 23 valued parcels, the rest ordinary 4,500 sqft townhouse lots at a normal $18/sqft, sharing a 1.07-acre HOA open space). Merging the mixed case would hand the whole HOA open space to 8 units that do not own it — the failure run_lynchburg.py guards against with its 'common-area parcels never chain' rule.

1,388 unit-sized parcels stay individual because NO common-area land is mapped in their plat at all — the development's land is simply absent from the county layer (e.g. 825 N 900 E units 1-6, six 580 sqft stubs at $94,500 each and nothing else in plat 55191). There is no key to merge them onto; 80 fall under the sub-500-sqft remnant filter and the rest render hot but bounded (p99 $77/sqft as rendered).

One genuine assessor anomaly ships as-is: serial 20:028:0023, an 899 sqft 'Vacant' fragment carrying $315,300 of land ($350/sqft) in an otherwise 12-50 acre rural block east of town. Both the polygon and the county's own acreage agree it is that small, so this is the Hartford '0 OLIVE ST' class of record — the assessor's own number, published unchanged rather than invented away (Seattle Westlake Center precedent).

CLASSIFICATION KEYS ON THE BUILDING TYPE, NOT THE ASSESSOR CLASS. PROP_CLASS is unusable alone: 14,665 Provo rows come back 'Unknown' (the LIR translation has no mapping for Utah County's condo/townhome/multi-unit codes) and Utah files non-primary residential under 'Commercial' because it is taxed at the full rate, so a duplex rented to students reads Commercial. BLDG_SQFT_INFO instead carries a rich 152-value taxonomy (int:_two_story = interior townhouse unit, 12_unit_building, fourplex:_two_story, storage_warehouse, ...), so categorize() uses the LARGEST building's type and only falls back to PROP_CLASS/HOUSE_CNT where the sole structure is accessory (shed, carport, detached garage). 104 parcels (0.6%, $59.6M land) land in 'Other' where neither signal is usable.

Baked to PMTiles + H3 despite being well under the ~100k-parcel rule of thumb — small GeoParquet cities render sparse when zoomed out (the Olympia 2026-07-01 lesson), and Provo's condo/townhome stock makes small parcels an unusually large share. Baked with --drop-remnants to match hideRemnants.

The source layer carries ~0.6% of overlapping area between large rural parcels (59 acres of 9,278 shipped, biggest single overlap 76.8k sqft between two 40+ acre parcels east of town). That is inherited county topology noise, not a merge artifact — no merged condo development is involved in any of the largest overlaps.

Parking is OSM-only but DID classify cleanly (unlike richmond/lynchburg/duluth, where the Overpass or Overture step failed): 267 lots / 221.4 acres / ~$150.9M estimated land value, split 259 surface / 6 structure / 1 uncertain / 1 excluded. Undercounts like every OSM-only city — the NAIP+ML satellite path was not run — and Utah County's LIR PROP_CLASS scheme has no surface-parking class, so there is no assessor figure to cross-check the undercount against.
